summary: iter-93 (Jan 2026) backend regression for the taxonomy / recharge / rails fixes — all 16 pytest cases PASS against the live preview backend. Verified: (1) `normalize_product_taxonomy` mirrors `sub_category` ↔ `subcategory` on BOTH vendor and admin create AND partial update (category-only PATCH preserves the mirror); (2) a Recharge product with sub_category='Airtel' derives recharge_kind='mobile' + recharge_network='airtel' server-side, sub_category='Tata Play' derives recharge_kind='dth' + recharge_network='tata-play', vendor-supplied recharge_state is persisted, and recharge_state='' is stored as None; (3) GET /recharge/products?kind=mobile&state=…&network=airtel gates a vendor plan behind admin publish, hides it for a different circle, and the seeded Airtel plans still list (iter-91 regression); (4) GET /products/{id}/rails rail[0] uses the sub-category $or match, and the guest rail-2 fallback stays INSIDE the parent's sub-category while sub-siblings remain (12-sibling case) and widens to the category only when the sub is empty (lonely-sub case); (5) /recharge/payment/start + /verify complete end-to-end with pay_MOCK_* ids even when `state` and `network` are omitted from the start call (hero-card path), and verify is idempotent; (6) shop-category cascade browse (?category=Recharge) and GET /shop-categories/tree still nest Recharge → Mobile Recharge → Airtel; (7) ordinary (non-Recharge) products are untouched by the normaliser — no recharge_* fields leak, cod_available / cashback_pct / variants survive.
critical_code_review_comments: core/taxonomy.py (ln 41-49): the mirror reads from `base` only when BOTH `subcategory` AND `sub_category` are absent from the incoming payload — exactly right. A PATCH that sends `sub_category: ''` would deliberately clear it; a PATCH that omits both keeps the stored value. Verified by test_vendor_update_category_only_preserves_mirror.

core/taxonomy.py (ln 72-73): the default `recharge_kind='mobile'` fallback is applied ONLY when the existing row ALSO has no kind — safe for admin PATCHes to a Recharge row that only tweaks price (the fallback does not clobber the already-stored kind).
core/taxonomy.py (ln 76-77): recharge_state='' → None conversion is the right lever because routes/recharge.py:393-397 treats missing/None recharge_state as 'available in every circle'. Verified.

routes/product_rails.py (ln 206-216): `sub_match` is a `$or` across both key shapes — resilient to legacy rows that only carry one shape, so the normaliser rollout does not need a one-off backfill to make rails work.

routes/product_rails.py (ln 246-260): fallback stays inside sub (`sub_match`) first and only widens to `cat` if the sub returns nothing beyond `rail_sub` + `product_id`. Verified by the 12-sibling populated-sub case AND the lonely-sub case.

routes/order_payments.py (ln 254-255): recharge start falls back to `plan.get('recharge_state')` / `plan.get('recharge_network')` when the client omits them — exactly what the product-hero-card Pay button relies on.

models.py / server.py — vendor still can't POST `subcategory` (only `sub_category` is a declared field on ProductCreate). This is the same cosmetic the iter-91 report called out. Not blocking (every active caller sends `sub_category`), but adding a pydantic alias would make the API shape symmetric with the normaliser. Not required for the fixes under test here.

success_rate.frontend: n/a (owner skipped FE automation this iteration)

seed_data_creation: Every product the suite creates is appended to `_CREATED_PRODUCT_IDS` and deleted via DELETE /api/admin/products/{id} in a module-scoped teardown. One recharge payment attempt + one `recharges` row are left behind for testbuyer@test.com (there is no admin recharge-delete endpoint); amounts are ₹49 on the mock Razorpay path, no money moved. The vendor's publish flag was flipped on test plans before cleanup — delete removes those docs. If the test_publish_gates test goes to create a second mobile state option (ITER93 Circle …), that option is left as `active=true` in `recharge_options` — a cosmetic leftover; it was NOT needed on every run because the preview DB already carries ≥2 states today.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public GET /api/products/{id} returns 404 for unpublished vendor products — use GET /api/vendor/me/products (vendor's own list) or GET /api/admin/products?limit=300 (paginated) to read freshly-created rows. The ADMIN product list endpoint ignores `?id=` and `?q=` id-match; walk pages instead. Login response field is `token` (not access_token), and the edge returns 403 for non-browser User-Agents — send `User-Agent: curl/8.5.0`. Preview backend is at EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL (not EXPO_BACKEND_URL — that key is absent in this frontend/.env).
rca_of_issue: No bugs found in the implementation under test. Two test-harness fixes applied while authoring: (a) `_get_admin_product` originally used GET /api/products/{id} which 404s for unpublished vendor products — rewrote as `_get_product_from_vendor_list` + `_get_product_from_admin_list` paginated readers; (b) rail-fallback test originally built only 3 sub-siblings, which rail-1 drained to 0 so the fallback legitimately widened to the category — rewrote with 12 siblings so the sub still has candidates after rail-1 picks 10, which is the actual invariant the owner asked us to protect.
